definitions.explanation: The biochemical stiffening of the muscles that occurs in a body within hours after death and gradually subsides over the next day or two. A key piece of evidence used in forensic medicine to estimate time of death.

examples.japanese: {遺体|いたい}に{死後硬直|しごこうちょく}が{始|はじ}まっていた。
examples.english: Rigor mortis had begun to set in on the body.

examples.japanese: {死後硬直|しごこうちょく}の{進行|しんこう}{具合|ぐあい}から{死亡|しぼう}{時刻|じこく}を{推定|すいてい}する。
examples.english: The time of death is estimated from the progression of rigor mortis.

examples.japanese: {死後硬直|しごこうちょく}は{通常|つうじょう}、{死後|しご}{二|に}〜{三時間|さんじかん}で{始|はじ}まる。
examples.english: Rigor mortis usually begins two to three hours after death.

examples.japanese: {死後硬直|しごこうちょく}は{筋肉|きんにく}{中|ちゅう}のATPが{枯渇|こかつ}することで{起|お}こる{現象|げんしょう}である。
examples.english: Rigor mortis is a phenomenon caused by the depletion of ATP in the muscles.

notes:
Composed of {死後|しご} (after death) and {硬直|こうちょく} (stiffening; rigidity). The compound is the standard medical and forensic term, with no commonly used native-Japanese alternative.

USAGE:
A technical term that appears chiefly in medical, forensic, and legal contexts: autopsy reports, crime fiction, news coverage of suspicious deaths, and biology textbooks. Outside of these contexts the word is rare in everyday conversation. The phenomenon itself is described with verbs like {始|はじ}まる (begin), {進|すす}む (progress), and {解|と}ける (be released, subside).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {死後硬直|しごこうちょく}が{始|はじ}まる: rigor mortis sets in
- {死後硬直|しごこうちょく}が{解|と}ける: rigor mortis subsides
- {死後硬直|しごこうちょく}の{進行|しんこう}: progression of rigor mortis
- {死後硬直|しごこうちょく}{時間|じかん}: the time period of rigor mortis

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {硬直|こうちょく}: stiffening; rigidity — the general term, also used metaphorically (e.g., {思考|しこう}の{硬直|こうちょく} 'rigidity of thought')
- {死斑|しはん}: livor mortis; postmortem lividity — another postmortem indicator used to estimate time of death
- {検死|けんし}: postmortem inspection of a body — the procedure in which rigor mortis is observed
- {遺体|いたい}: a (deceased) body — the object on which rigor mortis is observed
